newsitem.title: USA: Albright hails unity government in Angola.
newsitem.headline: Albright hails unity government in Angola.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright hailed Friday's inauguration of a government of national unity in Angola as "a milestone in ending over 30 years of conflict and bloodshed."
The ceremony was the culmination of a peace process that began in 1994 when the country's MPLA government and the rebel movement UNITA signed a pact in Lusaka, Zambia.
"I applaud both sides for their courage and perseverance in reaching this watershed point in the peace process," Albright said in a personal statement.

Angola was a major proxy battleground for the superpowers during the 1970s and 1980s, with the United States supporting UNITA against the Soviet- and Cuban-backed MPLA in a war that cost thousands of lives.
Washington dropped its support for UNITA after the Cold War ended.
Albright made no reference to the U.S. role in the conflict but said the United States had "made a strong commitment to helping end the war".
